project.name: Cosmos
project.description: Production-grade ERP and distribution platform with Vite+React frontend and Express+Prisma API backend on a single port

nodes.name: WarehouseTaskPage

nodes.name: WarehouseWaveDetailPage
nodes.summary: Mobile wave detail page showing pick path lines and task IDs, with buttons to start or complete the wave.

nodes.summary: Buyer notifications history page showing outbound notification events with filter and retry capabilities, resolved via JWT email.

nodes.name: BuyerNotificationsPage
nodes.summary: Notifications listing page that loads a buyer's notification history by email, supports filter by type, and allows retrying failed deliveries.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Order confirmation page displayed after successful checkout, showing order totals and line items with a link to the order detail page.

nodes.name: OrderConfirmationPage
nodes.summary: Post-checkout confirmation page that fetches and displays the newly created order details with a success message and link to full order view.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Order detail page for the storefront showing order lifecycle progress, shipment tracking, invoice status, line items, and reorder/cancel/confirm actions.

nodes.name: StorefrontOrderDetailPage
nodes.summary: Order detail page component showing the full order with a status stepper, shipment and tracking info, invoice link, and reorder/cancel/confirm actions.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Order history list page for the storefront that fetches paginated orders, supports B2B customer filtering, and provides one-click reorder.

nodes.name: StorefrontOrdersPage
nodes.summary: Orders listing page with B2B customer filtering, pagination, status badges, reorder action, and invoice link columns.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Quote detail page supporting buyer actions: view counter-offers, submit counter-offers, accept offers, request approval, and convert the quote to an order.

nodes.name: QuoteDetailPage
nodes.summary: Quote detail page that fetches a quote and its counter-offers, renders line items, and supports full quote negotiation and order placement workflows.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: New quote creation page that pre-populates line items from the B2B cart or URL params, allows editing, and submits a quote request to the API.

nodes.name: NewQuoteForm
nodes.summary: Quote form component that initializes from cart or query params, provides line-item editing with add/remove rows, and submits to the quotes API.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Quotes list page that fetches and displays the buyer's quotes with status badges, linking to each quote's detail page.

nodes.name: QuotesPage
nodes.summary: Quote listing page component that fetches all quotes for the current user and renders them in a table with status and navigation links.

nodes.name: cart.store.ts
nodes.summary: Zustand store managing the storefront shopping cart state including items, quantity updates, subtotal calculation, and add/remove/clear actions.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Zustand with a persist middleware pattern; exports useCartStore hook consumed by multiple page components.

nodes.name: checkout-card-capture.tsx
nodes.summary: Provides the StorefrontCardCapture React component that integrates with Stripe Elements to collect, validate, and tokenize credit card details at checkout.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Stripe's useStripe and useElements hooks with useCallback for form submission; no project-internal imports.

nodes.name: StorefrontCardCapture
nodes.summary: React component that renders a Stripe card input field and a save button; creates a Stripe PaymentMethod and returns its ID via a callback prop.

nodes.name: offline-banner.tsx
nodes.summary: Displays an offline status banner for mobile pages, showing pending queue length and providing a manual sync button that calls the offline queue replay logic.

nodes.name: OfflineBanner
nodes.summary: React component that listens to online/offline browser events and queue-change events, then renders connectivity status and a sync trigger button.

nodes.name: offline-sync-runner.tsx
nodes.summary: Minimal headless component that registers offline sync event listeners on mount; intended for use inside MobileLayout to set up background sync.

nodes.name: status-badge.tsx
nodes.summary: Renders a color-coded badge for ERP document statuses (orders, invoices, quotes) by mapping status strings to Tailwind CSS color classes.

nodes.name: StatusBadge
nodes.summary: React component that receives a status string and renders a styled span with color mapping for various ERP document lifecycle states.

nodes.name: api-mobile.ts
nodes.summary: Exports a pre-configured axios instance and helpers (api, gatewayApiBaseUrl, formatApiReachabilityError) for use in the mobile sub-application.

nodes.name: api.ts
nodes.summary: Exports a pre-configured axios instance (api) and associated helpers (gatewayApiBaseUrl, formatApiReachabilityError) used throughout the storefront client for API calls.

nodes.name: axios-error.ts
nodes.summary: Provides two utility functions: axiosErr for extracting a user-readable message from axios errors, and isUnauthorized for detecting 401 responses.

nodes.name: axiosErr
nodes.summary: Extracts a human-readable error message from an axios error response, handling array and string message formats.

nodes.name: isUnauthorized
nodes.summary: Returns true when an error is an axios 401 Unauthorized response, used to trigger re-authentication flows.

nodes.name: b2b-cart.ts
nodes.summary: Implements a localStorage-backed B2B quote cart with typed line-item validation, CRUD helpers, and a custom storage event to notify other components of cart changes.

nodes.name: readCart
nodes.summary: Reads and validates B2B cart line items from localStorage, returning a typed array with sanitized skuCode, description, qty, and unitPrice fields.

nodes.name: addToCart
nodes.summary: Adds a line item to the B2B cart or increments its quantity if the SKU already exists, then persists via writeCart.

nodes.name: offline-queue.ts
nodes.summary: Manages a localStorage-backed queue of offline actions (delivery/warehouse events) with UUID-stamped entries, providing enqueue, remove, clear, and length helpers.

nodes.name: enqueueAction
nodes.summary: Appends a new typed action with a UUID and ISO timestamp to the offline queue in localStorage and dispatches a storage event to notify components.

nodes.name: offline-sync.ts
nodes.summary: Replays queued offline actions against the mobile API when connectivity is restored, and provides registerOfflineSyncListeners to hook into online/service-worker events.

nodes.name: replayOfflineQueue
nodes.summary: Reads all queued offline actions and replays each against the mobile API, removing successfully processed actions from the queue.

nodes.name: registerOfflineSyncListeners
nodes.summary: Registers event listeners on the window online event and service worker messages to automatically trigger offline queue replay when connectivity is restored.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: The customer account management page allowing users to view and update their profile, address, notification preferences, saved payment cards, and B2B order templates.

nodes.name: AccountPage
nodes.summary: Main account page component that fetches and edits customer profile data, notification preferences, saved cards, and B2B order templates via the API.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Shopping cart page that displays cart items with quantity editing and removal, shows a subtotal, and navigates to checkout or quote creation.

nodes.name: CartPage
nodes.summary: React page component that renders the shopping cart with line item management, subtotal display, and navigation to checkout or quote creation.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: SKU catalog page with server-side paginated search, category/warehouse/price filtering, sort controls, and add-to-cart functionality for the B2B storefront.

nodes.name: CatalogPage
nodes.summary: Full-featured SKU catalog React page with debounced search, multi-filter panel, sort controls, paginated API fetching, and cart integration.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Multi-step checkout page handling shipping address, payment method selection (saved cards or new Stripe card), tax calculation, and order placement with idempotency key.

nodes.name: CheckoutPage
nodes.summary: Multi-step checkout wizard that loads customer info, manages shipping/payment state, and submits the order with payment integration.

nodes.name: PaymentStep2
nodes.summary: Payment method selection step component supporting saved cards, new Stripe card capture, and pay-later options with order total summary.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Invoice detail page that displays line items, totals, and credit memos, and supports both manual and Stripe card payment flows with PDF download.

nodes.name: StorefrontInvoiceDetailPage
nodes.summary: Invoice detail page component that loads an invoice by ID, renders line items and balance summary, and provides payment and PDF download actions.

nodes.name: InvoicePayPanel
nodes.summary: Payment panel component supporting manual payment entry or Stripe card payment against an invoice balance.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Invoice list page that fetches and displays paginated invoices with status filter tabs, showing balance, amount, and due dates.

nodes.name: StorefrontInvoicesPage
nodes.summary: Invoice listing page with status filtering, pagination, and unauthorized-state handling, using the storefront API.

nodes.name: analytics.ts
nodes.summary: Provides daily KPI snapshot computation and dashboard analytics for the ERP, aggregating order revenue, inventory counts, pick metrics, and MSA compliance status into time-series snapshots.

nodes.name: rollupDaySnapshot
nodes.summary: Aggregates order and SKU data for a given UTC day into a persistent KPI snapshot record.

nodes.name: dashboardKpis
nodes.summary: Computes high-level dashboard KPIs by assembling today vs prior day order metrics, pick performance, and MSA status.

nodes.name: upsertSnapshot
nodes.summary: Validates and upserts an externally-provided daily KPI snapshot record, enforcing role-based access.

nodes.name: ap-bills.ts
nodes.summary: Handles accounts-payable vendor bill lifecycle including three-way match validation (PO, receipt, bill), bill creation from purchase orders, and payment recording with GL journal posting.

nodes.name: computeThreeWayMatch
nodes.summary: Performs three-way match validation comparing PO quantities, received quantities, and bill amounts to detect discrepancies.

nodes.name: runThreeWayMatch
nodes.summary: Loads bill and PO from database, runs three-way match computation, and persists match results to the vendor bill record.

nodes.name: createBillFromPurchaseOrder
nodes.summary: Creates or updates a vendor bill from a purchase order, computing landed cost allocations, posting PO receipt GL journal, and triggering three-way match.

nodes.name: recordBillPayment
nodes.summary: Records a partial or full payment against a vendor bill, updates balance and status, and posts the AP payment GL journal.

nodes.name: audit-log.ts
nodes.summary: Provides lightweight audit event creation and retrieval, writing structured action records with entity context to the database for compliance and traceability.

nodes.name: auditLog
nodes.summary: Creates a structured audit event record in the database with action, entity type, entity ID, user ID, and optional metadata.

nodes.name: backorders.ts
nodes.summary: Manages backorder lifecycle: reserves available stock across FEFO lot allocations, creates backorder lines for unmet demand, and fills open backorders when new stock arrives.

nodes.name: reserveLineWithBackorder
nodes.summary: Reserves as much stock as available across FEFO lot allocations and creates a backorder line for any unmet quantity, updating the order line item accordingly.

nodes.name: fillBackordersOnReceipt
nodes.summary: When new stock is received for a SKU/warehouse, fills pending backorder lines in order priority and triggers fulfillment tasks for newly satisfied orders.

nodes.name: bank-recon.ts
nodes.summary: Provides bank reconciliation capabilities: managing bank accounts, importing bank statement lines, matching unreconciled lines, and producing reconciliation summaries.

nodes.name: importStatementLines
nodes.summary: Validates the bank account exists and bulk-inserts bank statement lines within a transaction for later reconciliation.

nodes.name: reconcileStatementLine
nodes.summary: Marks a bank statement line as reconciled and updates the bank account's cleared balance within a database transaction.

nodes.name: barcode-labels.ts
nodes.summary: Generates printable barcode label HTML for a given SKU, supporting configurable quantity and using Code128-style barcode formatting.

nodes.name: billing.ts
nodes.summary: Manages Stripe-based subscription billing: creating checkout and portal sessions, applying plan changes from webhook events, and syncing plan status to the tenant and auth databases.

nodes.name: createCheckoutSession
nodes.summary: Creates a Stripe checkout session for a tenant upgrading to a paid plan, configuring success/cancel URLs and ensuring a Stripe customer exists.

nodes.name: handleBillingWebhookEvent
nodes.summary: Handles Stripe webhook events for subscription lifecycle changes, applying or downgrading tenant plans based on subscription status.

nodes.name: bin-locations.ts
nodes.summary: Provides CRUD operations for warehouse bin locations, supporting zone and aisle metadata used by WMS putaway and pick tasks.

nodes.name: buyer-context.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves buyer identity context from a session, distinguishing portal buyers from admin staff and providing helper functions to enforce buyer-scoped access and retrieve auth profiles.

nodes.name: compose.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the Celestial AI response composition module, verifying formatting of tool results and fallback reply generation.

nodes.name: compose.ts
nodes.summary: Composes AI assistant replies from structured tool execution results, formatting warehouses, orders, invoices, quotes, low-stock alerts, and catalog results into Markdown, with doc-based fallback replies.

nodes.name: composeFromToolResults
nodes.summary: Filters tool results that contain data and maps them through section formatters to build a unified Markdown reply.

nodes.name: buildDocFallbackReply
nodes.summary: Constructs a fallback Markdown reply from platform documentation chunks when tool results are empty, filtering technical docs for consumer-facing responses.

nodes.name: conversations.ts
nodes.summary: Manages Celestial AI chat conversation persistence: creating or retrieving conversations, appending messages, listing conversation history, and updating timestamps.

nodes.name: intent.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the Celestial AI intent detection module, verifying classification of user messages into tool selection intents.

nodes.name: intent.ts
nodes.summary: Pure intent detection module for the Celestial AI assistant — classifies natural-language messages into sets of ERP tool names using regex patterns for orders, invoices, inventory, quotes, and search.

nodes.name: detectIntent
nodes.summary: Classifies a user message into a set of ERP tool names by matching regex patterns for orders, invoices, quotes, catalog, search, low-stock, and warehouse queries.

nodes.name: llm.ts
nodes.summary: Provider-agnostic LLM client for the Celestial AI feature, supporting OpenAI-compatible APIs (Groq, OpenRouter), Google Gemini, Ollama local models, and a mock fallback for development and testing.

nodes.name: completeChat
nodes.summary: Routes a chat completion request to the configured LLM provider (OpenAI-compatible, Gemini, Ollama, or mock) based on environment configuration.

nodes.name: callOpenAiCompatible
nodes.summary: Sends a chat completion request to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Groq, OpenRouter, etc.) and returns the text response.

nodes.name: callGemini
nodes.summary: Calls the Google Gemini API for chat completion, converting chat history format and extracting the text response.

nodes.name: mockComplete
nodes.summary: Provides a deterministic mock LLM response for development/testing by generating formatted replies based on the tool block embedded in the system prompt.

nodes.name: orchestrator.ts
nodes.summary: Central Celestial AI orchestration layer: prepares chat context by running intent-detected tools and doc retrieval, dispatches chat or streaming LLM completion, persists conversation messages, and enforces feature-flag access.

nodes.name: prepareChat
nodes.summary: Validates feature flag access, resolves buyer identity, detects intent, retrieves docs and tool results, builds the full prompt context, and optionally pre-composes a direct reply.

nodes.name: chat
nodes.summary: Executes a non-streaming Celestial AI chat turn: prepares context, completes via LLM, finalizes reply, and persists results.

nodes.name: chatStream
nodes.summary: Executes a streaming Celestial AI chat turn, emitting SSE chunks for direct compose replies or incrementally streamed LLM content, then persists the completed conversation.

nodes.name: prompts.ts
nodes.summary: Constructs system and context prompts for the Celestial AI assistant, adapting tone and capabilities based on whether the session user is a portal buyer or admin staff.

nodes.name: tools.ts
nodes.summary: Executes named ERP data-fetch tools for the Celestial AI assistant, dispatching to orders, invoices, inventory, quotes, global search, low-stock alerts, and warehouse queries to populate context for LLM responses.

nodes.name: runTool
nodes.summary: Dispatches a named tool to the appropriate ERP service (orders, invoices, inventory, quotes, search, low-stock, warehouses) and returns structured result data with navigation links.

nodes.name: compliance-msa.ts
nodes.summary: Implements MSA (Manufacturer Sales Authorization) compliance reporting: configuring tenant DID settings, importing transactions, generating weekly MULTICAT EDI files, storing them, and submitting via EDI endpoint with automated cron support.

nodes.name: generateReportForTenant
nodes.summary: Aggregates weekly MSA transactions, builds the MULTICAT EDI file, hashes and stores the file, and creates an MSA report database record.

nodes.name: submitReportEdi
nodes.summary: Retrieves a pending MSA report, reads its file from storage, and POSTs it to the configured EDI endpoint, updating the report status on success or failure.

nodes.name: runMsaAutomationCron
nodes.summary: Cron entry point that generates, uploads, and submits pending weekly MSA reports for a tenant, collecting results and errors.

nodes.name: compliance-tax.ts
nodes.summary: Provides sales tax computation utilities — calculating tax amounts from rates, resolving per-order tax based on ship-to state with tenant-configured rate fallback, and recording tax liabilities.

nodes.name: credit-limit.ts
nodes.summary: Enforces customer credit limit checks before order placement, tracks outstanding credit usage, and provides release mechanics for cancelled or paid orders.

nodes.name: crm.ts
nodes.summary: Core CRM service providing customer and lead management: CRUD and bulk import for customers and leads, Kanban-style lead status tracking, lead-to-customer conversion, and customer activity logging.

nodes.name: listCustomersPaged
nodes.summary: Returns a paginated and optionally filtered list of customers with total count for cursor-based pagination.

nodes.name: createCustomer
nodes.summary: Creates a new customer record with address, credit limit, net terms, and contact details, normalizing all string fields.

nodes.name: importLeads
nodes.summary: Bulk imports lead records from external data, validating required fields and Kanban status values, collecting per-row errors.

nodes.name: convertLead
nodes.summary: Atomically converts a CRM lead to a customer record within a transaction, updating the lead status to CONVERTED.

nodes.name: customer-notification-prefs.ts
nodes.summary: Manages per-customer notification preference settings stored as JSON on the tenant organization record, providing read, patch, and gating functions to filter notification sends by channel and template.

nodes.name: db.ts
nodes.summary: Initializes and exports all named Prisma database client instances for the platform's 14 domain databases (auth, tenant, inventory, orders, CRM, storefront, WMS, dispatch, purchasing, payments, compliance, notifications, ledger, analytics).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses separate Prisma clients per domain database, enabling independent schema evolution across ERP domains.

nodes.name: demand-planning.ts
nodes.summary: Computes SKU demand forecasts from historical stock ledger outbound events, generating days-of-supply, reorder recommendations, and suggested PO quantities for demand planning.

nodes.name: getSkuDemandPlan
nodes.summary: Computes a demand plan for a single SKU/warehouse including daily usage rate, days of supply remaining, and recommended reorder quantity based on lead time.

nodes.name: listDemandPlans
nodes.summary: Lists demand plans for all SKU/warehouse combinations, deduplicating and sorting by most critical days-of-supply to surface reorder priorities.

nodes.name: dispatch-order.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny utility module that extracts an order ID from a dispatch route stop's address field, used by the dispatch and order-shipments modules.

nodes.name: dispatch.ts
nodes.summary: Manages last-mile delivery route logistics including creating routes from orders, assigning drivers, recording GPS locations, reordering stops, and marking stops delivered or failed.

nodes.name: createRouteFromOrders
nodes.summary: Builds a delivery route automatically by looking up orders and their customer shipping addresses, then calling createRoute.

nodes.name: markStopDelivered
nodes.summary: Marks a route stop as delivered, fires the order orchestration delivery callback, and marks the entire route complete when all stops are done.

nodes.name: drop-ship.ts
nodes.summary: Handles drop-ship order flows: automatically creates supplier purchase orders for drop-ship line items and marks those lines shipped when the supplier confirms.

nodes.name: createDropShipPurchaseOrders
nodes.summary: Groups drop-ship line items by supplier and creates one purchase order per supplier, then marks the order lines with the resulting PO references.

nodes.name: markDropShipLinesShipped
nodes.summary: Records shipment for drop-ship lines, transitions the order status, and triggers invoice generation for the shipped quantities.

nodes.name: edi.ts
nodes.summary: Implements EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) integration: manages trading partners, ingests and processes 850 purchase order documents into native orders, and generates 810 invoice and 856 shipment notices.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dynamic imports for lazy loading of inventory and orders modules to avoid circular dependencies.

nodes.name: process850Document
nodes.summary: Parses and converts an EDI 850 purchase order document into a native ERP sales order, resolving customer and SKU references in the process.

nodes.name: feature-flags.ts
nodes.summary: Provides tenant-scoped feature flag lookups, returning enabled plan features and exposing an assertFeature guard that throws when a feature is not available.

nodes.name: inventory-lots.ts
nodes.summary: Manages inventory lot/batch tracking including creating and upserting lots, listing batches, FEFO-based batch allocation for picking, and per-SKU lot tracking settings.

nodes.name: allocateBatchesFefo
nodes.summary: Allocates inventory from batches using First-Expired-First-Out order by sorting stock levels by lot expiry date and greedily consuming available quantity.

nodes.name: inventory-serials.ts
nodes.summary: Handles serial number tracking for inventory items: registering new units, listing and reserving serials, shipping them against orders, and enforcing serial assignment at fulfillment time.

nodes.name: enforceAndShipSerialsForOrder
nodes.summary: Validates that all serial-tracked SKUs in a shipment have reserved serial numbers and marks those units as shipped.

nodes.name: inventory.ts
nodes.summary: Core inventory service managing SKUs, warehouses, stock levels, reservations, receipts, transfers, adjustments, and low-stock alerts across the entire platform.

nodes.name: receiveStock
nodes.summary: Posts a stock receipt for a SKU: upserts the stock level, creates a ledger entry, optionally handles lot association, and triggers backorder fill on completion.

nodes.name: reserveStock
nodes.summary: Creates a stock reservation for an order line, decrementing available quantity atomically and handling lot-tracked and serial-tracked SKUs.

nodes.name: commitShipmentForOrder
nodes.summary: Commits shipped inventory quantities against reserved stock levels, releases reservations, and posts stock ledger debit entries for the shipment.

nodes.name: adjustStock
nodes.summary: Posts a manual stock adjustment with an optional reason code, updating the stock level and writing a ledger entry.

nodes.name: invoice-gl.ts
nodes.summary: Posts accounts-receivable journal entries to the general ledger when invoices are issued and when credit memos are applied.

nodes.name: invoices.ts
nodes.summary: Full invoice lifecycle service: issuing invoices for orders, generating partial shipment invoices, synchronising invoice status from payment data, listing/getting invoices, recording payments, and applying credit memos.

nodes.name: issueInvoiceForOrder
nodes.summary: Creates an invoice record for an order, posts the AR journal entry, sends a notification to the customer, and triggers EDI 810 generation asynchronously.

nodes.name: applyCreditMemo
nodes.summary: Applies a credit memo against an outstanding invoice, updating balances, posting the credit memo journal entry, and handling partial and full credit scenarios.

nodes.name: ledger.ts
nodes.summary: General ledger service exposing journal entry CRUD (list, get, create draft, post), chart of accounts management, and a trial balance report grouped by account code.

nodes.name: trialBalance
nodes.summary: Computes a trial balance for a given year/month by aggregating journal line debits and credits per chart-of-accounts code.

nodes.name: native-router.ts
nodes.summary: The central API request dispatcher that routes all native HTTP requests to the appropriate domain handler modules, covering every ERP domain from inventory and orders to payments, WMS, dispatch, EDI, accounting, and AI.
nodes.languageNotes: Pattern-matches URL path segments in a giant switch/chain of route sub-functions; the only exported symbol is handleNativeApi. Imports 49 domain modules making it the integration hub.

nodes.name: handleNativeApi
nodes.summary: Top-level request handler that resolves the URL path to a specific route sub-function and returns the JSON response or appropriate error.

nodes.name: notification-triggers.ts
nodes.summary: Defines domain event notification triggers (order created, shipped, invoice issued, payment received, low stock) that check customer preferences before dispatching notifications via the notifications service.

nodes.name: notifications.ts
nodes.summary: Core notification delivery service: enqueues notification requests with idempotency, delivers via the notification provider, and supports listing and retrying failed notifications.

nodes.name: operations-gl.ts
nodes.summary: Posts operational general ledger journal entries for AR payments, AR refunds, PO receipts, AP payments, COGS recognition, and COGS reversals by resolving chart-of-accounts codes.

nodes.name: postArPaymentJournal
nodes.summary: Creates a double-entry journal entry for an accounts-receivable payment, debiting cash and crediting the AR account.

nodes.name: postCogsJournal
nodes.summary: Records a COGS journal entry debiting cost-of-goods-sold and crediting inventory asset when goods are shipped.

nodes.name: order-orchestration.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the order fulfillment saga pattern: orchestrates stock reservation, drop-ship PO creation, payment capture, WMS task creation, backorder handling, shipping, and order cancellation with compensation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a saga pattern with explicit step tracking in an orderSaga DB record to enable idempotent re-runs of the fulfillment pipeline.

nodes.name: runOrderFulfillmentPipeline
nodes.summary: Drives the full order fulfillment saga: reserves stock, creates drop-ship POs, triggers WMS fulfillment task creation, and transitions order status at each step.

nodes.name: cancelOrderWithCompensation
nodes.summary: Cancels an order with saga compensation: releases stock reservations, voids authorized payments, cancels WMS fulfillment tasks, and transitions the order to CANCELLED.

nodes.name: onFulfillmentDispatched
nodes.summary: Handles the dispatched fulfillment event: commits shipped inventory, posts COGS journal, triggers shipment invoicing, and marks short-picked lines as backordered.

nodes.name: order-payment-sync.ts
nodes.summary: Provides a lightweight utility to sync order payment totals from the payment ledger, keeping the order's amountPaid field consistent with actual recorded payments.

nodes.name: order-saga.ts
nodes.summary: Thin re-export barrel that exposes the order orchestration module as the public order saga entry point.

nodes.name: order-shipments.ts
nodes.summary: Manages order shipment records: listing and creating shipments, marking them shipped, and providing order tracking information including carrier and dispatch route stop data.

nodes.name: order-templates.ts
nodes.summary: Handles reusable order templates for storefront customers: CRUD operations and template-to-cart-line expansion with current pricing.

nodes.name: orders.ts
nodes.summary: Core sales order service managing order creation (with tax, pricing, credit limit checks), listing, confirmation, fulfillment, cancellation, payment recording, and reorder line generation.

nodes.name: createOrder
nodes.summary: Creates a new sales order after validating prices, checking credit limits, computing sales tax, and asynchronously kicking off the fulfillment pipeline and customer notification.

nodes.name: recordOrderPayment
nodes.summary: Records a manual payment against an order, updates the amountPaid field, releases credit exposure, syncs the invoice, posts the AR journal entry, and notifies the customer.

nodes.name: payment-idempotency.ts
nodes.summary: Provides idempotency key checking and registration for payment operations, preventing duplicate charge processing.

nodes.name: payments.ts
nodes.summary: Payment processing service integrating with Stripe: authorizes, captures, voids, and refunds payments; records payment and refund ledger entries; handles Stripe webhook events for async payment state updates.

nodes.name: handleStripeWebhook
nodes.summary: Verifies and processes inbound Stripe webhook events (payment_intent.succeeded, payment_intent.payment_failed, charge.refunded) updating payment intent state and posting corresponding ledger entries.

nodes.name: permissions.ts
nodes.summary: Defines role-to-permission mappings and provides hasPermission and assertPermission helpers used for fine-grained access control checks within API handlers.

nodes.name: pick-bin-resolver.ts

nodes.name: auth.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the complete authentication lifecycle for the ERP platform including login, registration, JWT token signing, refresh, logout, email verification, password reset, and invite acceptance using bcrypt and JOSE.

nodes.name: signPair
nodes.summary: Signs and returns an access+refresh JWT pair for a user, storing the bcrypt-hashed refresh token in the database for rotation validation.

nodes.name: loginUser
nodes.summary: Authenticates a user by email and password, enforces email-verification gate for new signups, updates lastLoginAt, and returns a signed token pair.

nodes.name: registerUser
nodes.summary: Creates a new user for a given tenant after validating the tenant exists and the email is unique, enforcing password policy and optionally issuing tokens or triggering email verification.

nodes.name: acceptInvite
nodes.summary: Validates an admin-issued invite token, registers the invited user with the associated role and tenant, and marks the invite as accepted.

nodes.name: sendEmailVerification
nodes.summary: Generates a 32-byte random email verification token, stores its SHA-256 hash with a 24-hour expiry, and delivers the verification email via the notification provider.

nodes.name: verifyEmail
nodes.summary: Validates an email verification token against its stored SHA-256 hash and expiry, then marks the user's email as verified.

nodes.name: requestPasswordReset
nodes.summary: Generates a 30-minute password reset token stored as a SHA-256 hash and sends the reset link by email without revealing whether the address exists.

nodes.name: resetPassword
nodes.summary: Validates the password reset token, enforces the password policy on the new password, re-hashes it, and invalidates all existing sessions by clearing the refresh token hash.

nodes.name: changePassword
nodes.summary: Allows an authenticated user to change their password by verifying the current password, enforcing the new password policy, and invalidating existing sessions.

nodes.name: db-health.ts
nodes.summary: Provides database health check utilities that verify all required database environment URLs are configured and test live connectivity to the auth database.

nodes.name: checkDatabaseConnections
nodes.summary: Iterates all database environment URL keys to verify they are set, then performs a live ping against authDb and returns a structured health report with per-check status.

nodes.name: env.ts
nodes.summary: Exports typed accessors for JWT secrets from environment variables and a utility for constructing Postgres database URLs, plus a constant listing all required database URL environment keys.

nodes.name: signup.ts

nodes.name: handleApiRequest

nodes.name: apply-prisma-provider.mjs

nodes.name: db-urls.mjs

nodes.name: databaseUrlForSchema

nodes.name: postgresDatabaseUrl

nodes.name: migrate-all.ts

nodes.name: Dockerfile

nodes.languageNotes: Uses three named stages (deps, builder, runner) to keep the final image lean. The runner stage copies only compiled artifacts from the builder, then sets a non-root system user (cosmos) for security. Port 4000 is the single unified port for the Express+Prisma API and Vite static assets.

nodes.name: deploy-production.yml

nodes.name: deploy-staging.yml

nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors the production workflow but targets the staging EKS cluster and Kustomize overlay. Uses commit SHA as the image tag (rather than a semantic version) and has a shorter rollout timeout of 10 minutes. No failure alerting configured.

tour.title: Platform Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Cosmos is: a production-grade ERP and distribution platform that serves a Vite+React SPA and an Express+Prisma API backend on a single port (4000). This document covers the single-port architecture, two UI themes (Obsidian and Aurora), SQLite-for-dev / Postgres-for-prod database strategy, multi-tenant workspace model, and the quickstart commands you need to spin up the platform locally. Reading it first gives you the mental map for everything that follows.

tour.title: Frontend Entry & Router
tour.description: The React application bootstraps in main.tsx — it applies the stored theme, registers the service worker for offline PWA support, and mounts the root React tree. App.tsx wraps the entire tree in a Providers component (React Query client) before rendering AppRouter. The router.tsx file is the architectural map of every UI surface: it lazy-loads page components under four layout roots — the public shop, the admin dashboard, the mobile PWA, and unauthenticated pages — making it the single best file for understanding the scope of the frontend.
tour.languageLesson: React Router v6 uses lazy() with dynamic import() to code-split each page into its own chunk. This means the initial JS bundle is small and each route's code is only downloaded when a user navigates to it — a critical optimization for a large app like this ERP with 40+ distinct pages.

tour.title: Admin Shell & Layout System
tour.description: AdminLayout.tsx is the route-level wrapper that enforces authentication (via RequireAuth) before rendering the DashboardShell. The dashboard-shell.tsx is the workhorse: it implements the collapsible sidebar, mobile navigation overlay, derives the page title from the current route, and embeds the floating Celestial AI chat panel. The sidebar.tsx component reads tenant feature flags from the API to dynamically filter which navigation items are visible — so tenants on different plans see different capabilities. These three files define the structural skeleton that every admin page renders inside.

tour.title: Design Tokens & Theming
tour.description: Cosmos ships two complete themes — Obsidian (dark enterprise) and Aurora (light lavender) — implemented as CSS custom property sets in globals-theme.css. The globals.css entry point imports the theme, admin, and shop surface stylesheets in sequence. The theme.ts utility reads and writes the chosen theme key in localStorage, while index.html contains an inline script that applies the theme attribute before first paint to prevent a flash of the wrong theme. Understanding this layer explains why every component uses CSS variables rather than hardcoded color values.
tour.languageLesson: CSS custom properties (variables) enable runtime theme switching without JavaScript re-renders. Setting `data-theme='obsidian'` on the `<html>` element activates a different set of `--cosmos-*` property values, and every component that references those variables immediately reflects the new theme.

tour.title: Key Admin Pages
tour.description: The admin dashboard (admin/page.tsx) is the operational nerve center: it renders KPI bento cards with sparklines, donut charts, a recent-orders widget, and low-stock alerts — all pulling live data from the analytics and inventory APIs. The inventory page (admin/inventory/page.tsx) provides SKU listing, stock editing, adjustment modals, and spreadsheet import. The orders page (admin/orders/page.tsx) exposes search, status filtering, pagination, and inline order creation — each order linking to its detail page showing the fulfillment timeline and actions. Together these three pages demonstrate how the admin UI surfaces the core ERP business objects.

tour.title: API Server Entry Point
tour.description: The Express server starts in apps/client/server/index.ts — it serves the compiled Vite SPA for non-API routes and bridges all /api/* requests to the web app's fetch-based API router, adding security headers in one place. The actual routing logic lives in apps/web/server/api-router.ts, which handles authentication flows, analytics endpoints, rate limiting, and delegates all other domain requests to the native-router.ts. That native router is the central dispatcher covering every ERP domain from inventory and orders to payments, WMS, dispatch, EDI, and AI — making it the index of the entire backend API surface.
tour.languageLesson: This architecture uses a single-port design: the Express server in apps/client/server/index.ts serves both the static SPA files and proxies /api/* to the backend handler. This eliminates CORS issues in development and production, since UI and API share the same origin.

tour.title: Core Server Modules
tour.description: Four modules form the load-bearing core of the backend. db.ts is the most-imported file in the entire server layer: it initializes and exports all 14 named Prisma client instances — one per domain database (auth, tenant, inventory, orders, CRM, storefront, WMS, dispatch, purchasing, payments, compliance, notifications, ledger, analytics). session.ts provides JWT verification, role-assertion helpers, and an ApiError class used by every protected handler. orders.ts manages the full sales order lifecycle from creation through confirmation, fulfillment, and cancellation. inventory.ts covers SKUs, warehouses, stock levels, reservations, receipts, and low-stock alerts. Every other server module depends on at least two of these four.

tour.title: Order Fulfillment Saga
tour.description: Placing an order in Cosmos triggers a multi-step saga orchestrated by order-orchestration.ts: it reserves stock, creates drop-ship purchase orders for supplier-fulfilled lines, captures payment via Stripe, creates WMS pick tasks, handles backorders for unmet demand, and ships confirmed lines — with compensation logic to roll back each step if a later step fails. The order-status.ts module enforces this lifecycle as a strict finite state machine: a map of valid next-states means an order can never jump illegally from CONFIRMED directly to SHIPPED without passing through PROCESSING. These two files together explain how Cosmos maintains data consistency across its 14 separate databases without a traditional distributed transaction.
tour.languageLesson: The saga pattern replaces ACID transactions across service boundaries. Each step in order-orchestration.ts is paired with a compensating action (e.g., release stock reservation if payment capture fails). This ensures the system reaches a consistent state even when individual steps fail, without requiring a distributed two-phase commit.

tour.title: Celestial AI Subsystem
tour.description: The Celestial AI assistant is a hybrid RAG + live-data system implemented across five focused modules. orchestrator.ts is the entry point: it detects user intent, runs the relevant ERP data-fetch tools, retrieves relevant documentation chunks, assembles the LLM context, dispatches to the configured provider, and persists the conversation. intent.ts uses regex pattern matching to classify messages into tool selections without an LLM call. retrieval.ts implements the RAG layer: it chunks the six platform Markdown docs in docs/celestial/, scores chunks by keyword + synonym expansion, and returns the most relevant passages. tools.ts executes the actual ERP queries (orders, inventory, invoices, quotes, search). llm.ts is provider-agnostic: it supports OpenAI-compatible APIs (Groq, OpenRouter), Google Gemini, Ollama, and a mock mode for development.
tour.languageLesson: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) avoids fine-tuning by injecting relevant document chunks into the LLM prompt at query time. The retrieval.ts module scores chunks using TF-IDF-style keyword matching rather than vector embeddings, making it dependency-free and fast — a practical choice when the document corpus is small and well-structured.

tour.title: Data Schemas
tour.description: Cosmos separates its data into 14 domain-isolated Prisma schemas, each backed by its own database connection. The order schema defines the complete order lifecycle: orders, line items, backorders, sagas, invoices, credit memos, and shipments. The inventory schema covers stock ledger, stock levels, SKUs, warehouses, bin locations, reservations, lots, and serial units. The auth schema holds User and Tenant models with RBAC enums. The tenant schema manages multi-tenant organization lifecycle, Stripe billing, onboarding steps, invites, POS registers, and EDI trading partners. The init-databases.sql script bootstraps all 15 PostgreSQL databases at first deploy. This domain separation is the architectural decision that most distinguishes Cosmos from a monolithic ERP database.
tour.languageLesson: Prisma supports multiple separate schema files by running `prisma generate` with the `--schema` flag pointing to each domain's schema file. The apps/web/package.json `generate` script chains 14 such commands, producing 14 separate client packages under `@/generated/prisma-*` — one per domain database — preventing cross-domain queries at the type level.

tour.title: Shared Packages
tour.description: Four monorepo workspace packages provide cross-cutting capabilities to both the client and server. The @cosmos/types package (packages/types/src/index.ts) exports domain primitives shared across the entire codebase: Role, Plan, JwtPayload, AuthenticatedUser, OrderStatus, MoneyAmount, and ApiError. The @cosmos/ui package exports Button, Card, and StatsCard components plus the cn() Tailwind class-merging utility. The @cosmos/analytics-engine package provides cashflow forecasting (EWMA with seasonal deseasonalization) and IQR-based anomaly detection used in the admin dashboard. The @cosmos/web-gateway-client package provides an axios factory with auth interceptors used by both the admin and storefront API clients.
tour.languageLesson: npm workspaces allow packages in the monorepo to reference each other by name (e.g., `@cosmos/ui`) without publishing to a registry. The root package.json `workspaces` field tells npm to symlink them into node_modules, so any workspace can import another as if it were an external dependency.

tour.title: Infrastructure & CI/CD
tour.description: The Dockerfile uses a three-stage multi-stage build: the builder stage installs all dependencies and compiles the Vite+React client and Prisma types; the production stage copies only the compiled output into a minimal Node.js 20 Alpine image running on port 4000 as a non-root user. The docker-compose.production.yml orchestrates Postgres, Redis, and the app container, wiring all 14 domain database URLs as environment variables. For Kubernetes, the base manifests in infra/k8s/base/ define the namespace, ConfigMap, Secret, Deployment (2 replicas, health probes on /api/v1/health), and Service — with Kustomize overlays scaling to 3 replicas in production. The Terraform modules provision the full AWS stack: VPC, EKS (t3.medium nodes with optional GPU group), RDS PostgreSQL, ElastiCache Redis, and S3 for document storage. The CI workflow runs lint, tests, and a full build against a live Postgres 16 service container on every PR, then validates the Docker image builds before the deploy workflow pushes to ECR and rolls out to EKS.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use multiple FROM statements. The builder stage contains dev tools (TypeScript compiler, Prisma CLI) needed only at build time; the final stage starts fresh from a slim base image and COPYs only the compiled artifacts. This keeps the production image small (typically under 200MB) and free of build-time attack surface.
